children: The FTSE 100 edged up on Wednesday, outperforming its European peers thanks to gains in energy shares.
Oil majors Shell and BP rose 1.8% and 2.8%, respectively, due to a renewed advance in oil prices.
Defence stocks also performed well, with aerospace company BAE Systems up 1.9%, submarine contractor Babcock climbing 2.6%, and engine-maker Rolls-Royce rising 1.3%.
On the other hand, JD Sports tumbled more than 3% after maintaining its guidance, and trimming its outlook last month amid weakness in the trainer market.
Diageo fell around 0.8% after appointing Joanne Wilson, currently CFO of WPP, as its new chief financial officer from 2027.
Meanwhile, Airtel Money confirmed plans for a London listing that could become the city’s largest IPO since 2021.
On the data front, the UK Composite PMI eased to 51.7 in September, slightly under market expectations of 52.

title: FTSE 100 Edges Up on Wednesday
